at gøre ondt.explanation: "At gøre ondt" means "to hurt". To say which body part hurts, put the body part first: "Min fod gør ondt" (My foot hurts). To say where you have pain, use "have ondt i" (have pain in): "Jeg har ondt i maven" (I have a stomachache).

at gøre rent.explanation: "At gøre rent" means "to clean", literally "to make clean". To say you clean a room, put the room between "gør" (make) and "rent" (clean): "Jeg gør køkkenet rent" (I clean the kitchen).

at gøre sig umage.explanation: "At gøre sig umage" means "to make an effort". The word "sig" (oneself) changes with the person: "Jeg gør mig umage" (I make an effort), "Du gør dig umage" (You make an effort). To name what you put the effort into, add "med" (with): "Hun gør sig umage med maden" (She makes an effort with the food).

at gøre sit bedste.explanation: "At gøre sit bedste" means "to do one's best". The word "sit" (one's) changes with who does it: "Han gør sit bedste" (He does his best), "Jeg gør mit bedste" (I do my best).

en gaben.explanation: "En gaben" means "a yawn". It is built from the verb "at gabe" (to yawn). To say you yawn in class, use the verb: "Jeg gaber i timen" (I yawn in class).

en gade.explanation: "En gade" means "a street". To say children play in the street, use "på gaden" (in the street): "Børnene leger på gaden" (The children play in the street). To talk about a road between towns, use "en vej" (a road): "Vejen til Odense er lang" (The road to Odense is long).

en gadedør.explanation: "En gadedør" means "a street door". It is built from "gade" (street) and "dør" (door). The part "dør" is spelled the same as the verb "dør" (dies): "Fuglen dør" (The bird dies).

en gadekat.explanation: "En gadekat" means "a stray cat". It is built from "gade" (street) and "kat" (cat). To talk about a cat that lives with a family, use "en huskat" (a house cat): "Vi har en huskat" (We have a house cat).

en gadelygte.explanation: "En gadelygte" means "a streetlight". It is built from "gade" (street) and "lygte" (lantern).

en gaffel.explanation: "En gaffel" means "a fork". A very common phrase is "kniv og gaffel" (knife and fork): "Jeg spiser med kniv og gaffel" (I eat with a knife and fork).

en galakse.explanation: "En galakse" means "a galaxy". The galaxy that our sun is in is called "Mælkevejen" (the Milky Way), literally "the milk road".

en gallerist.explanation: "En gallerist" means "a gallery owner". It is built from "et galleri" (a gallery) and the ending "-ist", which names a person.

en galning.explanation: "En galning" means "a madman". It comes from the adjective "gal" (mad). To say someone drives wildly, use "som en galning" (like a madman): "Han kører som en galning" (He drives like a madman).

en gang.explanation: "En gang" means "a hallway". To say how many times something happens, the same word means "time": "Jeg har været der to gange" (I have been there two times).

en gang imellem.explanation: "En gang imellem" means "once in a while". It is built from "en gang" (one time) and "imellem" (between). To say you do something from time to time, use it in the sentence: "Jeg ringer til min bror en gang imellem" (I call my brother once in a while).

en gang om ugen.explanation: "En gang om ugen" means "once a week". To say how many times, change the number: "tre gange om ugen" (three times a week). To name a different period, change the last word: "en gang om dagen" (once a day).

en garage.explanation: "En garage" means "a garage". To say where the car is, use "i" (in): "Bilen står i garagen" (The car is in the garage).

en garanti.explanation: "En garanti" means "a warranty". When you give a personal promise, the same word means "a guarantee": "Der er ingen garanti for det" (There is no guarantee of that).

en gartner.explanation: "En gartner" means "a gardener". A place where a gardener grows plants to sell is "et gartneri" (a plant nursery): "Vi køber tomater fra gartneriet" (We buy tomatoes from the plant nursery).

en gate.explanation: "En gate" means "a gate", as at an airport where you board a plane. To talk about a gate in a garden, use "en låge" (a garden gate): "Haven har en grøn låge" (The garden has a green gate).

en gaveindpakning.explanation: "En gaveindpakning" means "a gift wrapping". It is built from "en gave" (a present) and "en indpakning" (a wrapping). To ask a shop to wrap a present, say: "Kan I pakke gaven ind?" (Can you wrap the present?)

en ged.explanation: "En ged" means "a goat". It is also in "gedeost" (goat cheese), built from "ged" and "ost" (cheese): "Jeg vil have gedeost på salaten" (I want goat cheese on the salad).

en gedde.explanation: "En gedde" means "a pike". To say you fish for pike, use "fiske efter" (fish for): "Vi fisker efter gedder i søen" (We fish for pike in the lake).

en genbrugsbutik.explanation: "En genbrugsbutik" means "a secondhand shop". It is built from "genbrug" (recycling) and "en butik" (a shop). To talk about a place for old furniture, do not use it; use "en genbrugsstation" (a recycling center): "Vi kører gamle møbler til genbrugsstationen" (We drive old furniture to the recycling center).

en genbrugsstation.explanation: "En genbrugsstation" means "a recycling center". It is built from "genbrug" (recycling) and "en station" (a station). To say where you take old furniture, say: "Vi kører gamle møbler til genbrugsstationen" (We drive old furniture to the recycling center).
